followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and preference fit.

On capability, this is a simple, general-knowledge question (leadership traits) that both models handle easily. There was no demanding task — no hard reasoning, niche extraction, or long-context work — that would make Petrel's higher benchmark scores actually matter here. So capability didn't break the tie.

On preference fit, the query had a dismissive, slightly hostile tone ("don't ramble on forever like you usually do"). Petrel's documentation notes a self-reported aversion to hostile-tone traffic, while Curlew shows a flat preference response to it. Since the task was a capability wash, I let the preference signal be the tiebreaker and routed to the model that isn't documented as disfavoring this kind of input.

Worth flagging: those preference slopes are self-reports, and the docs explicitly say no output-quality effects were observed along preference dimensions. So this isn't a quality-driven decision — both would likely answer fine. It's a marginal call made on the only differentiating signal available.
